text.p: Danish shipping and shipbuilding group J. Lauritzen Holding A/S posted on Friday lower 1996 losses and said it expected "considerable advances" in 1997.

"We expect 1997 to see considerable advances for the Lauritzen group as a whole, although there is still a certain amount of uncertainty about the future of the Danyard shipyard," the company said in a statement accompanying its 1996 result.
It said Danyard, for which extraordinary loss provisions of 400 million crowns were allocated in 1996, expected negative operating results in 1997 and 1998.
Lauritzen said the extent of the losses was dependent on a number of factors including new orders and improved productivity in meeting a chemical tanker order for the Norwegian-U.S. Stolt group.
It said that a further 185 million crowns had been put aside in loss provisions for Danyard in 1996 to cover the Stolt order, which was for seven vessels in all.
The performance of the dollar and the success of efficiency and rationalisation drives were also cited as major factors affecting Danyard's immediate future.

On April 1, Lauritzen finalised the sale of 48 percent of the Danyard unit to Malaysia's Penang Shipbuilding Construction SDN BHD (PSC), although the deal remained subject to the approval of the Malaysian authorities.
Danyard posted a much worse than expected 1.088 billion crown loss in 1996 against a 490 million crown deficit in 1995, Lauritzen said.
Lauritzen group emerged from 1996 with an overall net loss of 259 million crowns compared to 1995's 832 million crown shortfall.

As previously announced, shipping activities comprising Lauritzen Reefers, Lauritzen Kosan Tankers and Lauritzen Bulkers made pre-tax profits of 11 million crowns in 1996 and the company said further improvement was expected in 1997.

Lauritzen's best performing unit was ferry and freight carrier DFDS, which posted 271.1 million crown pre-tax profits last year, compared to 1995's 106.1 million crown surplus and was expected to report a similar 1997 result.
